hints: Focus on what makes the reaction faster, think surface area, concentration and temperature all together.
Experiment 1 has powder, 2.0 mol dm-3 acid and 35 C, so it has every speed advantage and must have the shortest time.
Compare the two slow chip experiments, then place the powder experiment 2 ahead of the chip experiment 4 to get the order fastest to slowest as 1, 2, 4, 3.
walkthrough:
**Recall what controls rate**

Great start, remember faster rate means shorter time to collect the same volume of $\text{CO}_2$. Three things matter here.

Higher surface area (powder > large chips), higher $\text{HCl}$ concentration, and higher temperature all increase collision frequency and successful collisions.

**Pick the fastest and slowest**

Experiment 1 uses $\text{CaCO}_3$ powder + $2.0\,\text{mol}\,\text{dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HCl}$ at $35^{\circ}\text{C}$. That is maximum surface area, maximum concentration and maximum temperature, so it is fastest, about 5 s.

Experiment 3 uses large chips + $1.0\,\text{mol}\,\text{dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HCl}$ at room temperature. That is minimum in all three factors, so it is slowest, about 95 s.

**Order the middle two**

Experiment 4 is large chips + $1.0\,\text{mol}\,\text{dm}^{-3}$ at $35^{\circ}\text{C}$. Warming it makes it faster than experiment 3, so about 30 s.

Experiment 2 is powder + $2.0\,\text{mol}\,\text{dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HCl}$. Powder and double the concentration give a much bigger boost than temperature alone, so it is faster than experiment 4, about 10 s.

$$ \text{time: exp 1 (5 s) < exp 2 (10 s) < exp 4 (30 s) < exp 3 (95 s)} $$

options.A: This swaps experiments 3 and 4. Experiment 4 is at 35 C while experiment 3 is at room temperature, with surface area and concentration the same, so experiment 4 must be faster and have the smaller time, not 95 s.
options.B: This gives 5 s for experiment 1 (fastest), 10 s for experiment 2 (second), 30 s for experiment 4 (third) and 95 s for experiment 3 (slowest). It correctly shows powder faster than chips, 2.0 mol dm-3 faster than 1.0 mol dm-3, and 35 C faster than room temperature.
options.C: This makes experiment 4 the second fastest at 10 s and experiment 2 slow at 30 s. That is backwards because powder with 2.0 mol dm-3 acid (experiment 2) must react faster than large chips with 1.0 mol dm-3 acid (experiment 4), even allowing for temperature.
options.D: This reverses the whole trend, making experiment 1 slowest at 95 s and experiment 4 fastest at 5 s. It confuses faster rate with longer time. Remember, faster rate means less time to collect the same volume of CO2.
